plan: This is a second-price auction with 3 bidders and independent uniform values on [0,49]. The dominant strategy in a second-price auction is to bid your true value, since you pay the second-highest bid regardless of your own bid (as long as you win). Bidding true value ensures you win whenever profitable (value > others' bids) and never overpay. My value is $4, which is low, so I should bid $4 and likely lose to higher-value bidders, avoiding any loss.

This is a second-price auction with independent private values uniformly distributed on [0,49]. In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy: since you pay the second-highest bid (not your own bid) if you win, bidding your value ensures you win whenever profitable (value > second-highest bid) and avoid losses otherwise. There's no incentive to shade the bid. With no prior history to suggest otherwise, I'll bid exactly my value of $23.

This is a second-price auction with private values. In this format, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy: it maximizes expected profit regardless of others' bids, since you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid. Bidding above value risks paying more than value; bidding below value risks losing profitable wins. With no history to adjust for opponents' behavior, I'll bid exactly my value of $32.
